current_answer: Microsoft’s updated application guide excludes Series C or later and shows USD 200 at no-code entry versus USD 1,000 with an Investor Network code. Its older live activation guide still says USD 1,000 without a code. Confirm the actual no-code balance and account eligibility before planning Azure spend; credits are not cash.

catalogue_card.question: Is the Microsoft no-code startup credit USD 200 or USD 1,000?
catalogue_card.text: The newer application guide says USD 200 without an investor code, but an older live activation guide still says USD 1,000. The newer guide also excludes Series C and asks for a personal Microsoft account with no prior Azure account. Check your actual balance before deployment.

summary: The 9 October application guide lists pre-seed through Series B; Microsoft’s overview also excludes Series C or later.
The newer guide shows USD 200 without an investor code and USD 1,000 with one; the older activation guide still says USD 1,000 without a code.
The guide asks applicants to prepare a personal Microsoft account with no prior Azure account and payment details; sponsorship converts to pay-as-you-go after use or expiry.
uncertainty: Two live Microsoft guides still disagree on the no-code starter amount and do not establish an applicant-specific credit validity period.
The no-prior-Azure-account preparation line does not establish every account-history exception or guarantee approval.
Older programme rows keep their dated verification limits.
freshness_note: Microsoft application, activation and overview pages checked 15 October 2026. Other catalogue entries retain their dated checks.
